title: Ten-generation macromolecular autonomy
open: Sustain at least ten growth–division generations of a bottom-up cell that internally renews its proteins, ribosomes, genome, and membrane using only specified small-molecule nutrients and energy.
status: The July 2026 SpudCell preprint reports five generations with feeding and mechanical division; genetically dependent division was demonstrated separately. Complete macromolecular autonomy remains open.
why: Establishes reproducible construction of autonomous cellular reproduction.
key_works: Gaut et al. (2026), [A Chemically Defined Synthetic Cell Capable Of Growth And Replication](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.735724), preprint.

title: Purification-free renewal of the complete PURE proteome
open: Continuously replace every nonribosomal PURE protein through repeated dilution without purification or external enzyme replacement.
status: Mottaghi and Maerkl synthesized all 36 proteins together in 2026 and recovered functional PURE after purification; continuous internal renewal remains unresolved.
why: Removes a major external maintenance dependency.
key_works: Mottaghi and Maerkl (2026), [PURE makes PURE: reconstitution of the PURE cell-free system from self-synthesized proteins](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73337-0).

title: Chemically defined ribosome biogenesis
open: Produce functional ribosomes from an enumerated purified-component system with all necessary assembly, processing, and modification factors identified.
status: Kosaka et al. achieved coordinated ribosomal RNA and protein expression with functional assembly in cell extract in 2025; undefined extract activities prevent a molecular sufficiency claim.
why: Identifies the machinery needed for translation to reproduce itself.
key_works: Kosaka et al. (2025), [Autonomous ribosome biogenesis in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-55853-7).

title: Translation-component stoichiometry under self-regeneration
open: Derive and implement feedback rules maintaining functional translation-component ratios despite unequal synthesis, degradation, and partitioning.
status: Localized simultaneous production of 30 translation proteins was demonstrated in 2026; functionality remains sensitive to dilution and spatial organization.
why: Prevents failure through depletion of one indispensable component.
key_works: Schwarz-Schilling et al. (2026), [Autonomous biogenesis of all thirty proteins of the Escherichia coli translation machinery](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67772-8).

title: Demand-responsive synthetic tRNA pools
open: Adjust individual synthetic tRNA abundances to changing codon demand while maintaining measured translation fidelity and throughput.
status: All 21 minimal tRNAs were expressed from one template in 2025; position-dependent abundance and unregulated expression remain limitations.
why: Enables program changes without exhausting particular decoding resources.
key_works: Miyachi et al. (2025), [Simultaneous in vitro expression of minimal 21 transfer RNAs by tRNA array method](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62588-y).

title: Minimal tRNA maturation and modification requirements
open: Determine the processing and modification steps sufficient for accurate translation of an entire synthetic-cell proteome.
status: Continually transcribed minimal tRNA sets sustained reporter translation in 2025; proteome-wide accuracy and maturation sufficiency remain unestablished.
why: Tests whether simplified decoding systems support complete cellular reproduction.
key_works: Li, Baranwal, and Maerkl (2025), [Continuous in situ synthesis of a complete set of tRNAs sustains steady-state translation in a recombinant cell-free system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61671-8).

title: Reliable segregation of a synthetic genome
open: Deliver every required genetic component to both daughters with a quantified low loss rate over repeated divisions, without selecting successful daughters afterward.
status: The 2021 synthetic-cell-cycle roadmap identified segregation as an integration bottleneck; separate replication and division modules do not establish reliable inheritance.
why: Converts DNA replication into stable cellular lineages.
key_works: Olivi et al. (2021), [Towards a synthetic cell cycle](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-24772-8).

title: Complete FtsZ-driven vesicle scission
open: Couple internal FtsZ constriction to complete membrane scission while preserving daughter contents and repeated division capability.
status: Large equatorial FtsZ rings constricted vesicles to almost complete closure in 2026; reproducible final neck scission remains distinct.
why: Supplies an internally controlled mechanical division module.
key_works: Panevska et al. (2026), [Optimizing spatial organization of FtsZ rings for large-scale constriction in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70091-1).

title: Feedback between genome copying and membrane growth
open: Make DNA replication and membrane production regulate one another so genome dosage and cell size remain bounded through repeated cycles.
status: Expression, DNA self-replication, and lipid synthesis were integrated in vesicles in 2026; coordinated multigeneration control remains open.
why: Prevents overreplication, membrane starvation, and size drift.
key_works: Restrepo Sierra et al. (2026), [A synthetic cell with integrated DNA self-replication and lipid biosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69531-9).

title: One-chromosome replication at synthetic-cell genome scale
open: Faithfully copy one chromosome encoding the complete chosen synthetic-cell program fast enough to replenish genomes during growth.
status: Self-encoded DNA replication in liposomes dates to 2018; SpudCell’s 2026 program is multipartite, leaving single-chromosome integration open.
why: Reduces assortment failures and simplifies inheritance.
key_works: Van Nies et al. (2018), [Self-replication of DNA by its encoded proteins in liposome-based synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-03926-1); Gaut et al. (2026), [SpudCell preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.735724).

title: Homeostatic membrane composition
open: Preserve prescribed lipid ratios through continued growth despite changing precursor supply, enzyme abundance, and selective lipid loss.
status: Genetically controlled, metabolically balanced membrane synthesis was demonstrated in 2020; multigeneration composition control remains a stronger requirement.
why: Lipid composition controls permeability, curvature, and protein activity.
key_works: Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5).

title: Self-renewing membrane protein insertion
open: Regenerate membrane proteins and their insertion machinery while preserving orientation, folding, activity, and density during membrane expansion.
status: DNA-directed membrane-enzyme synthesis is established; a membrane proteome that renews its own assembly machinery over generations remains open.
why: Enables sustained transport and energy conservation.
key_works: Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5).

title: Coupled osmotic, ionic, and pH homeostasis
open: Simultaneously control volume, ionic strength, and pH during nutrient uptake, expression, and waste accumulation.
status: Energy-coupled physicochemical homeostasis was reconstructed in vesicles in 2019; integration with growing, genetically active cells remains unresolved.
why: Prevents otherwise functional modules from destabilizing one another.
key_works: Pols et al. (2019), [A synthetic metabolic network for physicochemical homeostasis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-12287-2).

title: Regeneration of an energy-producing artificial organelle
open: Sustain ATP production while internally replacing every protein and membrane component of the energy-transducing module.
status: Light-powered ATP production supported protein synthesis and partial component production in 2019; complete repeated renewal remains open.
why: Prevents exhaustion of the machinery powering cellular maintenance.
key_works: Berhanu, Ueda, and Kuruma (2019), [Artificial photosynthetic cell producing energy for protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09147-4).

title: Closed protein turnover and amino-acid recycling
open: Couple selective damaged-protein degradation to amino-acid reuse without destroying essential translation machinery.
status: Simultaneous synthesis and ClpXP degradation were demonstrated in cell-free systems in 2018; closed recycling and self-maintaining quality control remain additional requirements.
why: Enables sustained operation with bounded material inputs.
key_works: Shi et al. (2018), [Optimization of ClpXP activity and protein synthesis in an E. coli extract-based cell-free expression system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-21739-6).

title: Parasite-resistant protocell heredity
open: Determine experimentally validated conditions preserving cooperative genetic functions despite continuously arising faster-copying parasitic sequences.
status: Transient compartmentalization prevented parasite takeover in 2016; growing, heritable compartments introduce further assortment and selection constraints.
why: Makes protocell evolution compatible with persistent useful functions.
key_works: Matsumura et al. (2016), [Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aag1582).

title: Cell-level selection of multistep metabolic functions
open: Select complete multienzyme functions through their contribution to synthetic-cell reproduction while preventing improvements that merely exploit the selection readout.
status: Individual gene functions were linked to DNA replication and enriched in 2026; selection of complete pathway performance remains broader.
why: Enables evolutionary improvement of integrated synthetic-cell functions.
key_works: Sierra Heras and Danelon (2026), [Autocatalytic selection of gene functions in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10372-z).

title: Quantitative synthetic-cell module interfaces
open: Establish module descriptions that predict compatibility from resource demand, kinetics, inhibition, membrane coupling, and environmental tolerances.
status: The 2025 international synthetic-cell summit called for coordinated integration; no general experimentally validated compatibility calculus exists.
why: Makes independently developed modules composable.
key_works: Giaveri et al. (2025), [Building a Synthetic Cell Together](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62778-8).

title: Single-vesicle multigeneration accounting
open: Build a public benchmark jointly measuring inheritance, molecular replacement, membrane growth, division, and supplied resources in tracked lineages.
status: The 2026 Asian synthetic-cell roadmap proposes single-cell multi-omics and digital twins; cross-module measurements remain fragmented.
why: Makes autonomy claims quantitatively comparable.
key_works: Chinese Academy of Sciences (2026), [Asian Scientists Unveil 10-year Roadmap for Building Synthetic Cells](https://english.cas.cn/newsroom/research-news/202605/t20260528_1159994.shtml).

title: Complete functional annotation of essential minimal-cell proteins
open: Experimentally assign molecular functions and physiological roles to every remaining uncharacterized minimal-cell protein, with causal validation.
status: Annotation has advanced since JCVI-syn3.0’s 2016 construction; a 2026 analysis reports 50–60 previously unassigned proteins and proposes computational assignments requiring validation.
why: Turns a viable minimal genome into an understood one.
key_works: Mushegian et al. (2026), [Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0… encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors](https://doi.org/10.1128/msphere.00077-26).

title: Mechanisms of the minimal-cell division genes
open: Determine how poorly characterized JCVI-syn3A division genes cooperate with known division proteins, including their substrates and mechanical effects.
status: Seven genes jointly restoring regular division were identified in 2021; several lacked established molecular functions.
why: Explains how a genetically minimal cell divides reliably.
key_works: Pelletier et al. (2021), [Genetic requirements for cell division in a genomically minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.03.008).

title: Environment-indexed minimal genomes
open: Determine minimal viable gene sets for explicitly specified environments and predict required additions when conditions change.
status: A viable 473-gene genome was established in 2016; this is a demonstrated genome size, not a proven minimum.
why: Defines conditional requirements for life and robust chassis design.
key_works: Hutchison et al. (2016), [Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad6253).

title: Higher-order synthetic lethality in reduced genomes
open: Map and predict lethal or severely damaging combinations of individually dispensable deletions, including interactions among three or more loci.
status: The 2021 MiniBacillus compendium provides 105 progressively reduced genomes; this samples deletion trajectories rather than exhaustively mapping interactions.
why: Prevents unexpected failure during genome simplification.
key_works: Michalik et al. (2021), [The Bacillus subtilis Minimal Genome Compendium](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00339).

title: Predicting adaptation of minimized chassis
open: Predict compensatory mutations after genome reduction and whether adaptation preserves engineered production across environments.
status: Minimal cells recovered substantial fitness during 2,000 generations of evolution reported in 2023; trajectories and trade-offs remain difficult to predict.
why: Makes simplified production organisms evolutionarily predictable.
key_works: Moger-Reischer et al. (2023), [Evolution of a minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06288-x).

title: Prospective whole-cell prediction under genome redesign
open: Predict growth, morphology, and molecular responses to unseen genome edits before experiments, with calibrated uncertainty and no edit-specific fitting.
status: A complete spatial JCVI-syn3A cell cycle was modeled in 2026; broad prospective prediction under substantial redesign remains a stronger test.
why: Enables reliable design before expensive construction.
key_works: Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009).

title: Identifiable whole-cell parameter uncertainty
open: Determine which model parameters are identifiable and propagate unresolved uncertainty into engineered-phenotype predictions.
status: Whole-cell genotype-to-phenotype modeling dates to 2012; many parameters still rely on estimates or measurements borrowed from other contexts.
why: Distinguishes reliable predictions from nonunique fitted explanations.
key_works: Karr et al. (2012), [A Whole-Cell Computational Model Predicts Phenotype from Genotype](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2012.05.044).

title: Experimentally validated spatial inheritance distributions
open: Predict and measure joint distributions of molecular partitioning, chromosome configuration, and daughter physiology across generations.
status: The 2026 spatial whole-cell model predicts heterogeneous daughter states; testing joint distributions requires richer data than average doubling times.
why: Tests whether whole-cell models reproduce cellular variability.
key_works: Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009).

title: Complete Sc2.0 chromosome consolidation
open: Combine every designed Sc2.0 chromosome and the required tRNA complement in one stable strain retaining intended sequences and acceptable performance.
status: All 16 individual synthetic chromosomes exist; a 6.5-chromosome consolidated strain was reported in 2023, and 2026 consortium work still identifies full consolidation as unfinished.
why: Completes an integrated synthetic eukaryotic genome.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025).

title: Predicting interactions between synthetic chromosomes
open: Predict deleterious combinations of individually tolerated chromosome designs, including transcriptional, metabolic, and dosage interactions.
status: Systematic debugging exposed combinatorial defects during Sc2.0 consolidation in 2023; a general predictive interaction map remains absent.
why: Replaces repeated empirical debugging with prospective design.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025).

title: Stable dosage of a relocated tRNA genome
open: Preserve balanced tRNA expression after relocating the complete complement onto a designed chromosome, without selection for deletions or ploidy changes.
status: A roughly 190-kb neochromosome containing 275 tRNA genes was built in 2023; substantial dosage-related selection was observed.
why: Makes genome reorganization compatible with balanced translation.
key_works: Schindler et al. (2023), [Design, construction, and functional characterization of a tRNA neochromosome in yeast](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.10.015).

title: Predictable centromere placement
open: Determine the sequence, chromatin, and transcriptional conditions allowing reliable centromere function at a chosen location.
status: Relocated minimal yeast centromeres showed context-dependent activity and chromosome-copy effects in 2023.
why: Enables dependable chromosome architecture redesign.
key_works: Lauer et al. (2023), [Context-dependent neocentromere activity in synthetic yeast chromosome VIII](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100437).

title: Designer rDNA copy-number stability
open: Design rewritten or relocated rDNA arrays with predictable copy number, expression, recombination, and nucleolar function over extended growth.
status: Modified rDNA was regenerated at multiple locations in 2017; placement flexibility does not establish long-term quantitative stability.
why: Stabilizes a major repetitive and physiologically important genome region.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2017), [Engineering the ribosomal DNA in a megabase synthetic chromosome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf3981).

title: Faithful delivery of megabase mammalian constructs
open: Transfer megabase designs into diverse mammalian cells with predictable intactness, copy number, establishment efficiency, and unintended-change rates.
status: Efficient single-copy human artificial chromosome formation advanced in 2024; delivery across primary and differentiated cell types remains broader.
why: Enables large, coordinated mammalian genetic programs.
key_works: Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566).

title: Artificial-chromosome epigenetic portability
open: Maintain artificial-chromosome segregation and specified expression through cell-state transitions without dependence on a favorable initial epigenetic accident.
status: Single-copy formation improved in 2024; establishment and long-term epigenetic stability are separate requirements.
why: Makes chromosome-scale programs portable across differentiation.
key_works: Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566).

title: Defined biochemical bootstrapping of a synthesized genome
open: Identify a fully specified biochemical starting state sufficient to activate a synthesized cellular genome.
status: Synthetic-genome control after transplantation into an existing cell was achieved in 2010; a defined minimal molecular boot state was not established.
why: Separates genome design from inherited cytoplasmic organization.
key_works: Gibson et al. (2010), [Creation of a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesized genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1190719).

title: Prospective viability prediction for synonymous genome rewrites
open: Predict genome-wide synonymous replacement effects on fitness, RNA structure, expression, overlapping functions, and environmental responses before construction.
status: Multi-omics-guided debugging in 2026 revealed extensive molecular and condition-dependent effects in heavily recoded genomes.
why: Enables reliable large-scale sequence rewriting.
key_works: Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).

title: Conditional lower bounds on genetic-code compression
open: Prove a minimum codon count under specified decoding, growth, and fidelity constraints, or construct a smaller viable code.
status: A complete four-megabase E. coli genome using 57 codons, including 55 sense codons, was reported in 2025; optimality remains unproved.
why: Establishes physical and informational limits of translation architectures.
key_works: Robertson et al. (2025), [Escherichia coli with a 57-codon genetic code](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ady4368).

title: Hidden translated sequences in recoded genomes
open: Identify physiologically relevant translated sequences and alternative frames retaining supposedly removed codons, including condition-specific functions.
status: Annotation-related defects and unassigned codons were detected in extensively recoded genomes in 2026.
why: Prevents incomplete recoding caused by incomplete annotation.
key_works: Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).

title: Physiological termination with a compressed stop code
open: Preserve accurate termination, recycling, and stress responses across environments after reducing stop codons and altering associated factors.
status: An organism with one stop codon was engineered in 2025; broad physiological equivalence and portability remain open.
why: Makes code compression compatible with robust cellular function.
key_works: Grome et al. (2025), [Engineering a genomically recoded organism with one stop codon](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08501-x).

title: High-fidelity multiplex amino-acid incorporation
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Incorporate several distinct noncanonical amino acids into arbitrary proteins with measured positional fidelity, useful yield, and minimal host-proteome disruption.
status: Up to five distinct noncanonical amino acids were incorporated into a mammalian protein in 2026; sequence-general performance remains open.
why: Enables chemically richer proteins and multifunctional biologics.
key_works: Fang et al. (2026), [Recoding multiple rare codons enables the simultaneous incorporation of up to five distinct noncanonical amino acids](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02084-y).

title: Predictable quadruplet decoding in long proteins
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Predict quadruplet decoding efficiency and frameshift risk across sequence contexts and repeated sites in long proteins.
status: Work published in 2024/2025 reduced context dependence and identified 12 mutually orthogonal tRNA–synthetase pairs; general transfer remains unresolved.
why: Expands coding capacity without unpredictable synchronization errors.
key_works: Costello et al. (2024/2025), [Efficient genetic code expansion without host genome modifications](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-024-02385-y).

title: Full orthogonality of a parallel translation channel
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Quantify and minimize exchange of subunits, RNAs, and factors between engineered and native translation while retaining throughput.
status: Stapled orthogonal ribosomes constrained subunit interactions in 2018; this does not establish complete biochemical or resource isolation.
why: Allows independent evolution and operation of translation systems.
key_works: Schmied et al. (2018), [Controlling orthogonal ribosome subunit interactions enables evolution of new function](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0773-z).

title: Cell-state-robust modified-codon decoding
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Restrict modified-base codons to intended transcripts and retain decoding specificity across cell types, stresses, and endogenous modification changes.
status: Programmable pseudouridine-dependent decoding and mutually orthogonal pairs were demonstrated in mammalian cells in 2025.
why: Makes transcript-selective code expansion reliable.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [RNA codon expansion via programmable pseudouridine editing and decoding](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09165-x).

title: Predicting synthetase substrate confusion
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Predict synthetase discrimination among coexisting chemically similar substrates at physiological concentrations.
status: A 2025 simulation–experiment comparison covered a limited substrate panel; broadly calibrated catalytic-selectivity prediction remains open.
why: Prevents unintended monomer incorporation in expanded codes.
key_works: Lee and Choi (2025), [Predicting the polyspecificity of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase for non-canonical amino acids using molecular dynamics simulation and MM/PBSA](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0316907).

title: Long sequence-defined noncanonical backbone synthesis
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Manufacture long polymers with specified noncanonical backbone units at consecutive positions, verified fidelity, and practical isolated yield.
status: New ribosome-generated cyclic backbone motifs were demonstrated in 2025; arbitrary long-sequence synthesis remains beyond individual chemistry demonstrations.
why: Extends biological manufacturing into new polymer classes.
key_works: Lee et al. (2025), [Expanded ribosomal synthesis of non-standard cyclic backbones in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60126-4).

title: General consecutive D-amino-acid incorporation in vitro
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Translate finite peptides containing arbitrary contiguous combinations of bulky D-amino acids with predictable yield and low sequence bias.
status: Consecutive incorporation of nine bulky D-amino-acid types was demonstrated with an alternative ribosome in 2026; general sequence efficiency remains open.
why: Expands access to stable peptide scaffolds.
key_works: Katoh et al. (2026), [The Alteromonas macleodii ribosome enables consecutive incorporation of bulky D-amino acids into peptides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag341).

title: Affordable multiplex noncanonical amino-acid supply
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Economically synthesize several diverse noncanonical amino acids simultaneously and accurately incorporate them, reporting complete product-normalized costs.
status: A 2025 platform synthesized 40 aromatic amino acids and incorporated 19; broader chemistries and simultaneous production remain unfinished.
why: Removes precursor cost and availability bottlenecks.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2025), [A robust platform streamlining aromatic noncanonical amino acid biosynthesis and genetic code expansion in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63679-6).

title: Long-read, quantitative XNA sequencing
open: Sequence long, chemically diverse XNAs with calibrated substitution, insertion, and deletion errors while preserving modification information.
status: An XNA-adapted Sanger method read strands up to 50 bases in 2026; long reads and broad quantitative profiling remain open.
why: Enables measurement and evolution of alternative genetic polymers.
key_works: Wang et al. (2026), [Sanger Sequencing of Xeno-Nucleic Acid](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202516617).

title: High-fidelity long-XNA copying at physiological conditions
open: Copy long XNA templates under physiologically compatible conditions with sequence-dependent error rates low enough for repeated information retention.
status: Modified-nucleotide copying at 37°C advanced in 2026; short-template performance does not establish uniform accuracy across long sequences.
why: Supports sustained alternative-polymer heredity.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [Single-residue engineering of Klenow fragment enables broad acceptance of chemically modified nucleotides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697).

title: DNA-independent cell-free XNA heredity
open: Sustain cell-free XNA information transfer and selection without an obligatory DNA intermediate, with measured information capacity.
status: DNA-mediated XNA evolution was established in 2012; XNA-templated copying advanced in 2026, leaving sustained DNA-independent evolution open.
why: Tests whether alternative backbones can support independent heredity.
key_works: Pinheiro et al. (2012), [Synthetic genetic polymers capable of heredity and evolution](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1217622); Zhang et al. (2026), [Klenow-fragment engineering](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697).

title: Quantitative catalytic limits of XNA
open: Map efficiently accessible XNA reaction classes and determine whether catalytic repertoires systematically differ from DNA and RNA.
status: Multiple XNA chemistries yielded cleavage and ligation catalysts in 2015; their broader catalytic landscape remains unmapped.
why: Establishes functional possibilities and limitations of alternative polymers.
key_works: Taylor et al. (2015), [Catalysts from synthetic genetic polymers](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13982).

title: Predicting higher-order structures in expanded alphabets
open: Predict folding, mispairing, and functional structures of long nucleic acids containing more than four nucleotide letters.
status: Eight-letter hachimoji duplex thermodynamics and functional transcription were demonstrated in 2019; general long-sequence folding remains open.
why: Makes expanded alphabets designable beyond simple duplexes.
key_works: Hoshika et al. (2019), [Hachimoji DNA and RNA: A genetic system with eight building blocks](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0971).

title: Context-independent retention of unnatural base pairs
open: Predict unnatural-base-pair retention across sequence contexts and repeated copying while separating polymerase, chemical, and cellular error sources.
status: Cellular maintenance was demonstrated in 2014 and information retrieval in 2017; sequence-general reliability remains a broader target.
why: Enables dependable expanded genetic information.
key_works: Malyshev et al. (2014), [A semi-synthetic organism with an expanded genetic alphabet](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13314).

title: Economical manufacture of mirror-image binding proteins
open: Reproducibly manufacture finite D-protein binders at useful scale with lower synthesis, purification, and folding costs.
status: A functional mirror-image monobody was chemically synthesized in 2024; economical production across diverse sequences remains open.
why: Makes stable binding reagents and therapeutic candidates more accessible.
key_works: Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x).

title: Predictive disposition of finite mirror-image proteins
open: Build validated models of tissue distribution, clearance, accumulation, and immune interactions for finite mirror-image proteins.
status: Selected binding, stability, and biological responses were demonstrated in 2024; general pharmacokinetic and long-term disposition models remain absent.
why: Supports informed development of persistent molecular reagents.
key_works: Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x).

title: Predictive composition across hosts and environments
open: Predict assembled-circuit behavior across strains, media, temperatures, and growth phases with calibrated prospective uncertainty.
status: Cello automated construction in 2016; Cello 2.0 broadened support in 2022, while retaining characterized-library and deployment constraints.
why: Makes circuit reuse dependable.
key_works: Jones et al. (2022), [Genetic circuit design automation with Cello 2.0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00675-2).

title: Independent allocation of multiple cellular resources
open: Independently budget transcription, translation, folding, and degradation capacity while predicting residual coupling as bottlenecks change.
status: Dynamic orthogonal-ribosome allocation reduced two-gene coupling in 2018; simultaneous isolation across resource pools remains open.
why: Prevents one module’s demand from destabilizing others.
key_works: Darlington et al. (2018), [Dynamic allocation of orthogonal ribosomes facilitates uncoupling of co-expressed genes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-02898-6).

title: Burden feedback with specified productivity guarantees
open: Maintain specified output and host-growth envelopes under changing nutrient and expression demands.
status: Burden-responsive feedback was demonstrated in 2018; cross-stress guarantees remain construct-dependent.
why: Preserves useful production without exhausting the host.
key_works: Ceroni et al. (2018), [Burden-driven feedback control of gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4635).

title: Predicting resource-induced changes of circuit state
open: Predict when resource feedback creates or destroys stable states, oscillations, or switching thresholds, including rare-transition probabilities.
status: Resource competition redirected cascading cell-fate transitions experimentally in 2021; transferable quantitative boundaries remain unresolved.
why: Explains unexpected behavior after circuit integration.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2021), [Winner-takes-all resource competition redirects cascading cell fate transitions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21125-3).

title: Supercoiling-aware circuit layout
open: Predict transcriptional interference from gene order, orientation, spacing, and topological constraints well enough for prospective circuit layout.
status: Syntax-dependent supercoiling feedback and improved compact circuits were demonstrated in 2026; a general layout calculus remains open.
why: Makes sequence arrangement an explicit design variable.
key_works: Johnstone et al. (2026), [Gene syntax defines supercoiling-mediated transcriptional feedback](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adw1925).

title: Predictable relocation of genomic circuits
open: Preserve circuit behavior when moving between genomic loci, or predict necessary compensation before construction.
status: Highly insulated E. coli landing pads were demonstrated in 2020; arbitrary locus-to-locus portability remains unresolved.
why: Enables stable integration without repeated retuning.

title: Large orthogonal regulatory alphabets with measured limits
open: Determine how many regulatory channels can coexist at a specified error and burden budget, including higher-order interference.
status: Orthogonal repressor libraries have supported circuits since 2014; pairwise specificity does not establish collective capacity.
why: Defines realistic circuit scaling limits.
key_works: Stanton et al. (2014), [Genomic mining of prokaryotic repressors for orthogonal logic gates](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.1411).

title: Reliable asynchronous genetic logic
open: Compile circuits with explicit input-transition assumptions and bounds on transient errors under uncertain biological delays.
status: Hazard-aware genetic-circuit analysis and redesign were demonstrated in 2020; large-circuit stochastic guarantees remain open.
why: Prevents timing-dependent logical failures.
key_works: Fontanarrosa et al. (2020), [Genetic Circuit Dynamics: Hazard and Glitch Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.0c00055).

title: Wall-clock-stable biological oscillators
open: Maintain a prescribed elapsed-time period across growth, temperature, and load changes, with quantified phase diffusion.
status: Highly regular long-lived repressilator oscillations were demonstrated in 2016; broad environmental compensation remains open.
why: Enables dependable timing and scheduled cellular actions.
key_works: Potvin-Trottier et al. (2016), [Synchronous long-term oscillations in a synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19841).

title: Scalable rewritable memory in living cells
open: Build independently addressable cellular memory with measured capacity, write errors, retention, and rewrite endurance.
status: Rewritable memory was demonstrated in 2012; larger permanent memories followed, but capacity, reversibility, and reliability remain difficult to combine.
why: Enables persistent, updateable cellular state.
key_works: Bonnet, Subsoontorn, and Endy (2012), [Rewritable digital data storage in live cells via engineered control of recombination directionality](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1202344109).

title: Sequence diversification without functional drift
open: Remove repeated circuit sequences while preserving quantitative dynamics and reducing measured recombination and mutation failures.
status: Thousands of nonrepetitive parts were designed automatically in 2020; whole-circuit equivalence and lifetime gains remain broader tests.
why: Improves stability without sacrificing intended behavior.
key_works: Hossain et al. (2020), [Automated design of thousands of nonrepetitive parts for engineering stable genetic systems](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0584-2).

title: Prospective prediction of circuit evolutionary lifetime
open: Predict time-to-failure distributions from circuit sequence, host, expression, and cultivation history, then validate prospectively.
status: A 2025 computational study predicted over threefold half-life gains for some controllers; cross-design experimental lifetime prediction remains open.
why: Turns evolutionary stability into a measurable design specification.
key_works: Byrom and Darlington (2025), [Genetic controllers for enhancing the evolutionary longevity of synthetic gene circuits in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63627-4).

title: Quantitative cotranscriptional RNA design
open: Predict complete RNA-regulator response curves from sequence, folding kinetics, ligand association, and intracellular conditions.
status: General riboswitch-sensitivity tuning mechanisms were identified in 2025; intracellular states and transferable quantitative prediction remain uncertain.
why: Makes RNA regulation predictable from design.

title: Deep composable RNA logic
open: Cascade many RNA-processing stages while preserving signal, low leakage, and predictable timing; establish depth and fan-out limits.
status: A 12-input ribocomputing device was demonstrated in 2017; wide input integration does not establish deep composability.
why: Enables complex RNA programs assembled from reusable stages.
key_works: Green et al. (2017), [Complex cellular logic computation using ribocomputing devices](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature23271).

title: Scalable orthogonal RNA trans-splicing
open: Expand simultaneous trans-splicing regulators while predicting mis-splicing, leakage, and stoichiometry across transcript contexts.
status: SENTRs supported up to six-input logic in 2025; higher-dimensional interference and portability remain open.
why: Expands programmable processing of cellular RNAs.
key_works: Gao et al. (2025), [Programmable trans-splicing riboregulators for complex cellular logic computation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01781-4).

title: Independently programmable RNA lifetime
open: Specify transcript lifetime independently of translation, localization, and regulatory function across host states.
status: Degradation-tuning RNAs provided a 40-fold stability range in E. coli in 2021; broad transcript and host portability remains open.
why: Makes circuit timing independently adjustable.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2021), [Predictable control of RNA lifetime using engineered degradation-tuning RNAs](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-021-00816-4).

title: Interchangeable RNA-trigger-to-effector transduction
open: Convert intended RNA inputs into activated noncoding-RNA outputs with predictable specificity, amplification, and leakage across input–output combinations.
status: UNBAR demonstrated several effector classes in January 2026; universal interchangeability and large multi-device operation remain open.

key_works: Lim et al. (2026), [A programmable ribozyme for RNA signal transduction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-68175-5).

title: General discovery of useful small-molecule RNA sensors
open: Produce selective intracellular sensors for specified diverse ligands with a known success rate and useful response range.
status: DRIVER automated multiplexed biosensor evolution in 2021; broad ligand coverage with prospective guarantees remains unresolved.
why: Expands the chemical inputs accessible to living circuits.
key_works: Townshend et al. (2021), [A multiplexed, automated evolution pipeline enables scalable discovery and characterization of biosensors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21716-0).

title: Portable RNA logic between translation systems
open: Transfer RNA computations between prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems with predictable changes in thresholds, leakage, and timing.
status: Eukaryotic toeholds were demonstrated in 2021/2022; successful distinct architectures leave a general portability framework open.
why: Makes RNA design libraries reusable across organisms.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2022), [RNA-responsive elements for eukaryotic translational control](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01068-2).

title: RNA generative design outside the training distribution
open: Generate regulators for new structural families, sensing regimes, and cellular contexts with calibrated uncertainty and prospective validation.
status: SANDSTORM/GARDN generated functional candidates from relatively small datasets in 2025; reliable mechanistic extrapolation remains open.
why: Extends design beyond interpolation among familiar sequences.
key_works: Riley et al. (2025), [Generative and predictive neural networks for the design of functional RNA molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59389-8).

title: Large protein-logic libraries with collective orthogonality
open: Design protein components that remain mutually specific when coexpressed, including unintended assemblies and sequestration.
status: Orthogonal heterodimers appeared in 2019 and protein Boolean gates in 2020; collective scaling remains open.
why: Enables larger, faster post-translational programs.
key_works: Chen et al. (2019), [Programmable design of orthogonal protein heterodimers](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0802-y).

title: Reusable deep proteolytic circuits
open: Repeatedly process changing inputs through multistage proteolytic circuits while replenishing components and preventing interference from cleavage products.
status: Composable regulated-protease circuits were demonstrated in 2018; sustained resettable operation introduces additional constraints.
why: Converts one-time cleavage logic into reusable computation.
key_works: Gao et al. (2018), [Programmable protein circuits in living cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat5062).

title: Predictably wired phosphorylation networks
open: Connect reversible phosphorylation modules while preserving transfer functions and timing despite shared enzymes, saturation, and endogenous interactions.
status: Modular synthetic phosphorylation networks were established in human cells in 2025; extensive scaling and portability remain open.
why: Enables rapid analog and dynamic computation.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), [Engineering synthetic phosphorylation signaling networks in human cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adm8485).

title: Specified allosteric response functions
open: Design protein assemblies with prescribed cooperativity, thresholds, hysteresis, and switching kinetics while preserving output activity.
status: Allosterically switchable assemblies were designed in 2024; arbitrary quantitative response programming remains unestablished.
why: Makes protein behavior programmable beyond binding affinity.
key_works: Pillai et al. (2024), [De novo design of allosterically switchable protein assemblies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07813-2).

title: Low-cost insulation from downstream molecular load
open: Minimize downstream-load effects on upstream dynamics while bounding energy, bandwidth, and component costs.
status: A yeast phosphotransfer load driver was demonstrated in 2014; general low-cost insulation across variable loads remains open.
why: Preserves module behavior after connection.
key_works: Mishra et al. (2014), [A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3044).

title: Learning within protein neural circuits
open: Demonstrate an intracellular learning rule that adapts a protein classifier from feedback while preserving earlier useful classifications.
status: Perceptein circuits demonstrated tunable winner-take-all classification in 2024; onboard learning remains a separate target.
why: Enables adaptive cellular decision-making.
key_works: Chen et al. (2024), [A synthetic protein-level neural network in mammalian cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.add8468).

title: Integral control with variable dilution and resource constraints
open: Achieve specified tracking error and stability under simultaneous growth dilution, resource changes, and actuator saturation.
status: Sensor-based antithetic control improved speed and noise experimentally in 2026; combined physiological guarantees remain open.
why: Makes cellular regulation robust outside narrowly tuned conditions.
key_works: Filo et al. (2026), [Engineering sensor-based antithetic integral controllers for enhanced dynamic performance and noise attenuation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2025.101512).

title: Robust control of entire single-cell distributions
open: Maintain specified output distributions, rare tails, and temporal correlations under changing reaction rates and environments.
status: Theory and simulations of simultaneous mean and noise adaptation appeared in 2025/2026; full-distribution experimental control remains broader.
why: Controls clinically or industrially important rare-cell behavior.
key_works: Lim et al. (2026), [Toward single-cell control: noise-robust perfect adaptation in biomolecular systems](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67736-y).

title: Composable multivariable intracellular control
open: Independently regulate several outputs and ratios despite shared resources, with explicit stability and cross-coupling bounds.
status: Resource-aware multilayer autocatalytic models solved selected concentration and ratio-control tasks in 2025; general experimental designs remain open.
why: Enables coordinated control of complex cellular programs.
key_works: Zand et al. (2025), [Multi-Layer Autocatalytic Feedback Enables Integral Control Amidst Resource Competition and Across Scales](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.4c00575).

title: Attainable joint limits on control precision, speed, and cost
open: Derive tight joint bounds on noise, response speed, adaptation accuracy, and resource expenditure, and construct systems approaching them.
status: Molecular noise-suppression bounds date to 2010; subsequent trade-off results remain assumption-dependent.
why: Distinguishes engineering deficiencies from physical limitations.
key_works: Lestas, Vinnicombe, and Paulsson (2010), [Fundamental limits on the suppression of molecular fluctuations](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09333).

title: Experimentally useful observability and controllability tests
open: Determine whether available noisy sensors and constrained inputs permit practical state inference and control.
status: Structural analyses of selected nonlinear synthetic circuits appeared in 2024–2025; finite-data and model-uncertainty guarantees remain open.
why: Identifies when additional sensors or actuators are necessary.
key_works: Pardo et al. (2024), [Analysing control-theoretic properties of nonlinear synthetic biology circuits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05450), arXiv:2411.05450.

title: Single-cell control without measurement distortion
open: Control fast intracellular dynamics while accounting for reporter maturation, delay, phototoxicity, and sensing burden.
status: Deep predictive control reached thousands of individual cells in 2024; high-bandwidth control of nonproxy outputs remains open.
why: Makes measured control correspond to the biological quantity of interest.
key_works: Lugagne, Blassick, and Dunlop (2024), [Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46361-1).

title: Verified circuit guarantees despite model discrepancy
open: Produce probabilistic guarantees valid under parameter uncertainty, unmodeled host interactions, and measured model discrepancy.
status: Stochastic hazard verification was demonstrated with iBioSim and STAMINA in 2021; transferring guarantees to uncertain living implementations remains open.
why: Connects formal verification to actual biological reliability.
key_works: Buecherl et al. (2021), [Stochastic Hazard Analysis of Genetic Circuits in iBioSim and STAMINA](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00159).

title: Synthetic signaling near measured information limits

status: Intrinsic limits for biochemical motifs were analyzed in 2018; experimental attainment with realistic dynamic inputs remains open.
why: Establishes how efficiently cells can sense and communicate.
key_works: Suderman and Deeds (2018), [Intrinsic limits of information transmission in biochemical signalling motifs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6227803/).

title: Robustly tunable synthetic Turing patterns
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization

key_works: Tica et al. (2024), [A three-node Turing gene circuit forms periodic spatial patterns in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2024.11.002).

key_works: Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Predictive mechanical coupling in patterning circuits
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Predict spatial outcomes jointly from signaling, growth, crowding, adhesion, and mechanical boundaries.

key_works: Santorelli et al. (2024), [Control of spatio-temporal patterning via cell growth in a multicellular synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53078-8).

subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization

title: Compilation from temporal specifications to working circuits
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Compile pulses, delays, adaptation, and memory specifications into feasible circuits with prospective timing and burden guarantees.
status: Cello 2.0 formalized Boolean design and deployment in 2022; general experimentally validated temporal compilation remains open.

subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries

why: Makes automated experiments portable.

title: Reproducible workflows across independent biofoundries
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Transfer complete DBTL workflows between differently equipped facilities while preserving performance within predefined tolerances.

why: Enables substantial molecular redesign without losing manufacturability.

title: Specified innervation of engineered tissues
open: Produce predetermined neural connections to engineered tissues and verify selective, stable functional control.
status: Functional cortico-motor assembloids were reported in 2020; prescribed wiring and mature long-term control remain open.
why: Enables integrated neuromuscular and organ function.
key_works: Andersen et al. (2020), [Generation of Functional Human 3D Cortico-Motor Assembloids](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.11.017).

title: Tissue repair to a programmed stopping condition
open: Restore specified tissue size and cell proportions after repeated injury, then reliably return proliferation and loss to homeostatic balance.
status: Simple structures self-repaired in 2018; quantitative size restoration with reliable growth arrest remains open.
why: Enables regeneration without progressive overgrowth or lineage depletion.
key_works: Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Plant-autonomous nitrogen fixation with net agronomic benefit
open: Supply a meaningful fraction of cereal nitrogen demand through internal fixation without a larger energy or growth penalty.
status: Plant-produced NifB supported cofactor synthesis in vitro after cluster reconstitution in 2022; this did not demonstrate nitrogen fixation inside plants.
why: Could substantially reduce fertilizer dependence.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2022), [Functional Nitrogenase Cofactor Maturase NifB in Mitochondria and Chloroplasts of Nicotiana benthamiana](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.00268-22).

title: Predictable fertilizer replacement by engineered root symbionts
open: Predict fertilizer displacement and yield across soils, climates, genotypes, and management with independently verified nitrogen budgets.
status: Engineered diazotrophs already show field activity; partial replacement was reported in 2024, while site-specific reliability remains open.
why: Makes biological nitrogen provision agronomically dependable.
key_works: Martinez-Feria et al. (2024), [Genetic remodeling of soil diazotrophs enables partial replacement of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with biological nitrogen fixation in maize](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-78243-3).

title: Integrated C4 photosynthesis in rice
open: Combine anatomy, cell-specific expression, transport, and enzymatic activity into functional C4 rice with measured yield advantage.
status: Pursued since the 2000s; bundle-sheath regulatory logic advanced in 2025, leaving full integration unfinished.
why: Could improve carbon assimilation and resource efficiency.
key_works: Hua et al. (2025), [A transcription factor ensemble orchestrates bundle sheath expression in rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62087-0).

title: A complete chloroplast carbon-concentrating mechanism
open: Integrate carboxysomes, inorganic-carbon transport, and leakage control to improve net crop assimilation under ambient air.
status: Carboxysome-containing tobacco supported autotrophic photosynthesis at elevated CO₂ in 2023; complete ambient-air concentration remains open.
why: Improves photosynthetic carbon efficiency.
key_works: Chen et al. (2023), [Engineering α-carboxysomes into plant chloroplasts to support autotrophic photosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37490-0).

title: Photorespiratory bypasses with reproducible food-crop yield gains
open: Establish harvestable-yield gains across diverse food crops and environments while separating productivity from biomass repartitioning.
status: Tobacco field gains were demonstrated in 2019; rice paddy-field gains were reported online in 2025, leaving broad reproducibility open.
why: Converts pathway improvements into dependable food production.
key_works: South et al. (2019), [Synthetic glycolate metabolism pathways stimulate crop growth and productivity in the field](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat9077); Chen et al. (2025/2026), [Rice photorespiratory-bypass field study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cj.2025.03.001).

title: Fast photoprotection without stress vulnerability
open: Accelerate photoprotection recovery while retaining heat, drought, and sustained-excess-light resilience in reproducible field trials.
status: Recovery engineering improved productivity in 2016 and soybean yields in 2022; combined-stress consistency remains open.
why: Captures more fluctuating sunlight without sacrificing resilience.
key_works: Kromdijk et al. (2016), [Improving photosynthesis and crop productivity by accelerating recovery from photoprotection](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aai8878); De Souza et al. (2022), [Soybean photosynthesis and yield study](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adc9831).

title: Root programs that adapt to heterogeneous soil
open: Make root architecture respond predictably to spatial water and nutrient variation while preserving useful above-ground growth.
status: Synthetic circuits reprogrammed Arabidopsis roots in 2022; autonomous adaptation in elite crops and soil remains open.
why: Improves resource acquisition under variable conditions.
key_works: Brophy et al. (2022), [Synthetic genetic circuits as a means of reprogramming plant roots](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abo4326).

title: Plant memory that remains accurate through development
open: Record environmental events in intended lineages with quantified false records and losses over an entire crop life cycle.
status: Stable plant memory circuits were demonstrated in 2022; developmental fidelity and field-length validation remain open.
why: Enables reliable environmental recording and conditional development.
key_works: Lloyd et al. (2022), [Synthetic memory circuits for stable cell reprogramming in plants](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-022-01383-2).

title: Genotype-independent transformation and regeneration
open: Install complex programs in elite crop varieties and regenerate fertile plants without genotype-specific redevelopment or major abnormalities.
status: Morphogenic-regulator approaches continue expanding access; 2026 CRISPR-Combo results cover several perennial crops, not universal regeneration.
why: Removes a central barrier to crop engineering.
key_works: Ramasamy et al. (2026), [Boosting genome editing in perennial plants by CRISPR-Combo mediated morphogenic gene activation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-76367-w).

title: Portable chloroplast engineering across crop species
open: Transfer multigene plastid designs across species with predictable expression, inheritance, and pathway function.
status: A 2025 Chlamydomonas platform supplied over 140 regulatory parts; cross-crop transferability remains empirical.
why: Makes organelle design libraries broadly reusable.
key_works: Inckemann et al. (2025), [A modular high-throughput approach for advancing synthetic biology in the chloroplast of Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-025-02126-2).

title: Orthogonal plant-hormone control in the field
open: Achieve spatially selective development with predictable field dose–responses from engineered hormone–receptor pairs.
status: An orthogonal auxin–TIR1 pair was demonstrated in 2018; delivery, persistence, and agronomic selectivity remain open.
why: Enables externally adjustable plant programs.
key_works: Uchida et al. (2018), [Chemical hijacking of auxin signaling with an engineered auxin–TIR1 pair](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.2555).

title: Reliable synthetic apomixis across crops
open: Preserve hybrid genotypes through clonal seed formation across crops while maintaining fertility, germination, and multigeneration agronomic performance.
status: High-frequency synthetic apomixis was achieved in rice in 2022, followed by fertility advances; broad crop portability remains open.
why: Could preserve hybrid advantages through saved seed.
key_works: Vernet et al. (2022), [High-frequency synthetic apomixis in hybrid rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35679-3).

title: Predictable therapeutic-strain abundance in diverse human guts
open: Predict and control introduced-strain abundance across diets and resident communities without broad ecosystem disruption.
status: Dietary-niche control was shown in mice in 2018 and reversible human engraftment in 2025; cohort-general quantitative control remains open.
why: Makes living-medicine exposure predictable.
key_works: Shepherd et al. (2018), [An exclusive metabolic niche enables strain engraftment in the gut microbiota](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0092-4); Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000).

title: Therapeutic output that survives gut evolution
open: Maintain specified per-cell output during prolonged human colonization and predict the engineered function’s lifetime.
status: The 2025 controlled-colonization study documented genetic-stability challenges; strain persistence does not establish payload persistence.
why: Preserves therapeutic action after engraftment.
key_works: Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000).

title: Quantitative clinical interpretation of living gut diagnostics
open: Convert microbial recordings into calibrated estimates of disease timing, location, and severity while accounting for abundance and transit.
status: Long-term inflammatory sensing was demonstrated in mice in 2017; clinical sensitivity and specificity remain further requirements.
why: Turns biological recordings into interpretable diagnostics.
key_works: Riglar et al. (2017), [Engineered bacteria can function in the mammalian gut long-term as live diagnostics of inflammation](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3879).

title: Causal spatial models of engineered microbiomes
open: Predict metabolic and host-exposure changes caused by relocating or locally modifying community members, validated by spatial interventions.
status: MaPS-seq mapped microbial spatial associations in 2019; causal spatial design remains harder than measuring co-location.
why: Enables engineering beyond bulk community composition.
key_works: Sheth et al. (2019), [Spatial metagenomic characterization of microbial biogeography in the gut](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0183-2).

title: Knowing when pairwise community models fail
open: Establish testable conditions for reliable pairwise models and bound experiments needed to detect necessary higher-order interactions.
status: Pairwise modeling successfully described a defined gut community in 2018; general approximation limits remain unresolved.
why: Determines how much community complexity must be measured.
key_works: Venturelli et al. (2018), [Deciphering microbial interactions in synthetic human gut microbiome communities](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20178157).

title: Community evolution that optimizes a durable collective function
open: Predict when community selection yields persistent functional improvement rather than transient composition changes or noncontributor enrichment.
status: Directed-community-evolution frameworks advanced in 2021; general experimentally validated heritability rules remain open.
why: Enables evolution of useful ecosystem-level traits.
key_works: Chang et al. (2021), [Engineering complex communities by directed evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01457-5).

title: Selective recall of deployed living medicines
open: Remove a therapeutic population on demand across spatial refuges while preserving resident communities and preventing delayed rebound.
status: Controllable microbial removal was demonstrated in 2022; complete durable human recall remains a stronger criterion.
why: Makes persistent living medicines reversible.
key_works: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).

title: Surrogate endpoints that predict microbial-therapy benefit
open: Determine when strain biomarkers or metabolite conversion causally predict patient-important outcomes across doses and populations.
status: Phenylketonuria platforms progressed from 2018 development to a 2023 phase 2 report; general surrogate validity remains separate.
why: Improves trial interpretation and therapeutic development.
key_works: Isabella et al. (2018), [Development of a synthetic live bacterial therapeutic for the human metabolic disease phenylketonuria](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4222).

title: Plant-protective communities that generalize across soils
open: Design defined communities that reproducibly improve crop stress phenotypes across resident microbiomes and soil types.
status: Desert-rhizosphere communities improved tomato salt resilience in 2022; environmental transfer remains open.
why: Makes microbial crop protection dependable.
key_works: Schmitz et al. (2022), [Synthetic bacterial community derived from a desert rhizosphere confers salt stress resilience to tomato in the presence of a soil microbiome](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41396-022-01238-3).

title: Complete remediation of changing pollutant mixtures
open: Sustain contained treatment of variable pollutant mixtures while identifying major transformation products and closing contaminant mass balances.
status: Engineered degradation of multiple pollutants was demonstrated in 2025; mixture-general performance and by-product assurance remain open.
why: Establishes that contaminant disappearance reduces hazard.
key_works: Su et al. (2025), [Bioremediation of complex organic pollutants by engineered Vibrio natriegens](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08947-7).

title: Field-calibrated living environmental sensors
open: Infer analyte levels reliably across seasonal temperature, hydration, chemistry, and cellular-aging changes.
status: Remote bacterial sensing was demonstrated in 2017; operational calibration and maintenance remain open.
why: Enables dependable long-duration environmental monitoring.
key_works: Belkin et al. (2017), [Remote detection of buried landmines using a bacterial sensor](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3791).

title: Climate-resilient symbioses without hidden fitness costs
open: Predict when improved symbiont stress tolerance benefits hosts across their life cycle without unacceptable reproductive or ecological costs.
status: Heat-evolved algae improved coral bleaching tolerance experimentally in 2020; lifelong benefit and ecological transfer remain open.
why: Supports evidence-based conservation interventions.
key_works: Buerger et al. (2020), [Heat-evolved microalgal symbionts increase coral bleaching tolerance](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aba2498).

title: Integrated biological life support with closed material budgets
open: Integrate production, waste recycling, and resource recovery with quantified external inputs, failure recovery, and mission-level advantages.
status: A 2020 Mars-biotechnology roadmap articulated the opportunity; isolated demonstrations do not establish integrated mission-scale performance.
why: Reduces dependence on resupply in remote environments.
key_works: Nangle et al. (2020), [The case for biotech on Mars](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0485-4).

title: Predictive lifetime bounds for biological containment
open: Predict containment-failure probabilities across specified populations, generations, and environments with validated confidence intervals.
status: Strong laboratory synthetic dependencies were demonstrated in 2015; general lifetime prediction remains unresolved.
why: Converts isolated escape assays into interpretable reliability evidence.
key_works: Mandell et al. (2015), [Biocontainment of genetically modified organisms by synthetic protein design](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14121).

title: Containment of engineered DNA after cell death
open: Quantify and limit genetic-material persistence and functional transfer after engineered cells die.
status: Targeted DNA destruction was demonstrated in 2015; environmental fate and transfer assurance require broader evidence.
why: Addresses genetic-material behavior independently of cell viability.
key_works: Caliando and Voigt (2015), [Targeted DNA degradation using a CRISPR device stably carried in the host genome](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms7989).

title: Containment assays that capture dormancy and resuscitation
open: Standardize assays distinguishing death from temporary nonculturability and quantifying later resuscitation across physiological states.
status: Modern kill-switch systems provide test cases; shared assurance covering latent survival remains an infrastructure gap.
why: Prevents false confidence from culture-negative measurements.
key_works: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).

title: Independent, privacy-preserving synthesis-screening assurance
open: Independently evaluate screening sensitivity, specificity, privacy, and update reliability without disclosing sensitive sequences or customer designs.
status: SecureDNA reported operational screening at substantial scale in 2026; independent system-wide assurance and adoption remain separate challenges.
why: Supports trustworthy screening across providers.
key_works: Baum et al. (2026), [A system capable of verifiably and privately screening global DNA synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag103).

title: Bounding mirror-life risks without creating mirror organisms
open: Reduce ecological and immune-risk uncertainty using nonliving components, existing observations, and independently scrutinized models.
status: A 2024 assessment identified potentially severe risks and advocated against creating mirror bacteria; evidence-based risk bounds remain open.
why: Informs research restrictions and oversight without constructing the hazardous system.
key_works: Adamala et al. (2024), [Confronting risks of mirror life](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ads9158).

title: Durable global access to verified biological materials
open: Sustain affordable access to authenticated strains, plasmids, and standards, including preservation, documentation, replacement, and delivery.
status: Addgene reported expanded international distribution in 2026; access inequalities and long-term repository financing remain open.
why: Makes reproducible research possible beyond well-resourced centers.
key_works: Addgene (2026), [Strengthening Foundations: Reflections on 2025 and What’s Ahead for 2026](https://blog.addgene.org/strengthening-foundations-reflections-on-2025-and-whats-ahead-for-2026).

title: Funded capacity for locally chosen synthetic-biology priorities
open: Establish durable funding and technical support enabling under-resourced communities to choose, evaluate, and maintain their own applications.
status: CBD Decision 16/21 initiated capacity-building work in 2024; its 2025–2026 program ties activities to resource availability.
why: Transfers operational capability and local decision-making power.
key_works: Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).

title: Comparable evidence for environmental decisions
open: Develop interoperable evidence packages covering function, persistence, reversibility, ecological effects, and uncertainty while retaining local relevance.
status: CBD’s 2024 decision provides an institutional starting point; universally validated experimental criteria remain absent.
why: Improves comparability and scrutiny of environmental decisions.
key_works: Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).
